name: Haikou
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Haikou: Hainan Free Trade Port counterparties, bonded zone trade, duty-free retail and IP court disputes.
hero_lede: Investigative consulting for matters touching Haikou, scoped from Nashville: background research on companies formed under the Hainan Free Trade Port regime, diligence on trading and logistics counterparties around the customs-separated island, and factual support for counsel in intellectual property and foreign-related commercial disputes heard in Haikou.
intro: Haikou is the capital of Hainan Province and the administrative and commercial centre of the Hainan Free Trade Port. The island began island-wide special customs operations in December 2025, with a separate customs regime, zero-tariff import lists and an exemption for goods processed on the island with at least 30 percent added value. Over the five years to 2025 Hainan reported more than 100 billion yuan of actual foreign investment and more than 8,000 new foreign-invested enterprises. Haikou hosts the Haikou Comprehensive Bonded Zone, the Jiangdong New Area, Xinhai and Xiuying ports, Meilan International Airport and the Haikou International Duty-Free City, and is the seat of the province's principal courts and government bodies.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Haikou because the free trade port has attracted many newly formed companies, often with short operating histories, offshore parents or holding structures set up to use preferential tax and trade rules. Buyers and lenders need to know who stands behind trading, logistics and duty-free supply companies, and whether goods and value-added processing are what they are claimed to be. Brand owners face counterfeit and grey-market risks around duty-free retail. Foreign parties in disputes may find themselves before Haikou's specialised intellectual property and foreign-related commercial tribunals, where counsel need well-documented facts about the other side and its assets.

matters.title: Free trade port company backgrounds
matters.text: Researching companies newly registered in Haikou to use free trade port tax and trade incentives, including shareholders of record, offshore parents, related entities, registered address and real operations, so investors and counterparties can judge whether a company has substance or is a shell created for a single transaction.

matters.title: Zero-tariff and value-added claims
matters.text: Testing, through public records, trade information and where justified site checks by qualified local professionals, whether Haikou processors and traders carry out the processing they claim, supporting buyers and compliance teams concerned about origin, transshipment and misuse of the island's tariff exemptions.

matters.title: Duty-free supply chain diligence
matters.text: Background research on distributors, agents and suppliers serving Haikou's duty-free retail sector, covering ownership, litigation, administrative penalties and adverse media, to help brand owners and investors identify parallel trading, counterfeit risk and conflicts of interest among intermediaries.

matters.title: IP infringement research in Hainan
matters.text: Supporting counsel in trademark, copyright and patent matters by identifying the companies and individuals behind suspected infringement on the island, their related entities and assets, and assembling publicly documented facts for proceedings before the Haikou or Hainan Free Trade Port intellectual property courts.

matters.title: Asset and counterparty research for disputes
matters.text: Locating lawfully documented assets, related companies and enforcement history of Hainan-registered counterparties for foreign parties pursuing claims before Haikou's foreign-related commercial tribunal or in arbitration, and identifying where a debtor's business may have been moved into new entities.

local_context.title: Haikou intellectual property courts
local_context.text: The Haikou Intellectual Property Court was established on 26 September 2019 within the Haikou Intermediate People's Court to centralise IP jurisdiction across the province. In its first year the Hainan courts handling IP accepted 1,720 cases, including 29 foreign-related cases with right holders from the United Kingdom, South Korea and Italy. A separate court named after the Hainan Free Trade Port began accepting civil, administrative and criminal IP cases in January 2021.

local_context.title: Foreign-related commercial tribunal
local_context.text: In September 2019 Hainan set up two cross-regional tribunals for first-instance civil and commercial cases involving foreign, Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan parties, with one in Haikou. They hear disputes up to 5 billion yuan and were described as the first provincial-level cross-regional special tribunals of their kind in China. Their records help show a counterparty's history of cross-border disputes.

local_context.title: Hainan International Arbitration Court
local_context.text: The Hainan International Arbitration Court is described in the provincial investment guide as the only civil and commercial arbitration body established by the Hainan provincial government. Foreign investors in free trade port projects may encounter it in dispute clauses. We have not verified its address or caseload; arbitral awards are not generally public, so diligence relies on court enforcement records and other lawful sources.

local_context.title: Registration and customs administration
local_context.text: Business start-up, registration and cancellation in Hainan run through the province-wide Hainan E-Registration platform, alongside national market regulation records. Since December 2025 goods moving between Hainan and the mainland pass through second-line customs checkpoints, and a smart customs supervision platform supports zero-tariff and value-added trade, producing a separate layer of trade compliance that bears on counterparty diligence. Diligence takes both layers into account.

tdsc_approach: For matters touching Haikou, TDSC first defines the question, whether that is a new free trade port company's substance, a processor's value-added claims, a duty-free intermediary's links or a debtor's assets, and then identifies the relevant records, including Haikou court decisions, provincial administrative penalties and registration data. Research is conducted from Nashville using Chinese-language open sources, published judgments and trade information, together with offshore records where Hainan entities have foreign parents. Where site visits or document retrieval are justified, TDSC coordinates with qualified local professionals and the client's Chinese counsel. Personal information is collected only as needed, and any transfer of data out of China is reviewed with counsel first.

faqs.q: How do we check whether a Haikou-registered company has real operations?
faqs.a: We compare the registration record, business scope, registered capital and address with tax-incentive eligibility claims, hiring and trade activity, litigation and penalties, and any offshore parent records. Many free trade port entities are recent, so we look closely at who formed them and what they did before. Where needed, qualified local professionals can carry out lawful site observations.

faqs.q: Can you help verify claims about zero-tariff or value-added processing?
faqs.a: We can research the processor's ownership, facilities, permits, trade history and disputes through lawful sources and identify inconsistencies with its claims. We cannot access customs systems or confidential declarations. Where processing claims are central to a transaction or dispute, we recommend counsel obtain documents through contract rights or formal procedures.

faqs.q: Which courts in Haikou hear foreign-related disputes?
faqs.a: Haikou hosts a cross-regional tribunal for first-instance civil and commercial cases involving foreign, Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan parties, set up in 2019, and intellectual property courts with province-wide jurisdiction. Which forum applies depends on the claim and contract, so counsel should confirm jurisdiction. We assemble facts about counterparties and their litigation history.

faqs.q: Are Hainan court judgments a complete record of a company's disputes?
faqs.a: No. They are useful, but publication of Chinese judgments has narrowed and arbitration outcomes are generally private. We combine judgments with enforcement, penalty and registration records and other public material, and we state clearly when the absence of a record cannot be treated as proof that no dispute exists.

faqs.q: Does TDSC have an office in Haikou?
faqs.a: No. TDSC is based in Nashville and has no office or staff in Haikou or elsewhere in China. Most work is desk-based research. Where on-the-ground steps are needed, we coordinate with qualified local professionals acting lawfully and with the client's Chinese counsel, and we decline requests involving restricted records or covert methods.
